quest.title: To Hear Mortal Hearts
quest.description: Ippei says that Kujou Kamaji has gone to see the head of the Takatsukasa Clan. Ei decides to go there personally to settle the issue of the Tenryou Commission's internal affairs. Thus, you and Ei head out into the wilds, toward the secret base of the Takatsukasa Clan...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x600, Primogem x60, Mora x38100, Guide to Light x5, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

talks.objective: Head to the Takatsukasa Clan's secret outpost

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, look at how well-hidden this place is!

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: I can't think of a reason anyone would want to build a structure like this deep in the mountains.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: I feel something that doesn't belong here... I sense danger.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: We should proceed with caution. The Kujou Clan descendant may well be in trouble.

talks.objective: Reach the deepest area of the outpost
Talk to Kujou Kamaji and Takatsukasa Susumu

dialogues.speaker: Takatsukasa Susumu
dialogues.text: Almighty Shogun!

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
dialogues.text: Sh—Shogun, what are you...

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Descendant of the Takatsukasa Clan. Explain what is going on here.

dialogues.speaker: Takatsukasa Susumu
dialogues.text: Oh, we're just discussing some minor issues that have cropped up in the Tenryou Commission recently. Really, it's nothing worth the Almighty Shogun worrying about...

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: And these minor issues warranted the secluded location and the hiring of ronin and kairagi to keep guard?

dialogues.speaker: Takatsukasa Susumu
dialogues.text: Well, there's there's been a lot of turmoil lately. It was just out of security considerations, that's all...

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Silence.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Descendant of the Kujou Clan. Your turn.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
dialogues.text: Alright. I came here intending to negotiate, but it turned out all they were interested in was a written confession from the Kujou Clan.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: A written confession?

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
dialogues.text: Yes. A statement acknowledging every crime committed by the Kujou Clan since the inception of the Vision Hunt Decree, including all the recent misconduct...

dialogues.speaker: Takatsukasa Susumu
dialogues.text: All factual statements of course. Not a single one of them fabricated.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
dialogues.text: I can't deny that. But it also emphasizes the Takatsukasa Clan's achievements throughout the document, claiming that they stood steadfast all along and fought back against the crisis...

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
dialogues.text: These are all falsehoods.

dialogues.speaker: Takatsukasa Susumu
dialogues.text: Says who? Why, you two-faced...! You're going back on everything you said!

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
dialogues.text: I'm just stating the facts. I'm sure the Almighty Shogun can discern the truth. All the Takatsukasa Clan is trying to do is make themselves look good, so they'll be first in line to replace the Kujou Clan!

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
dialogues.text: Why else would you push a false narrative in the written confession that paints your clan in a good light? And try to make me sign it under duress?

dialogues.speaker: Takatsukasa Susumu
dialogues.text: What are you talking about? You're not under duress, we're just negotiating here! You've completely changed your tune!

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: I believe I now understand the situation.

dialogues.speaker: Takatsukasa Susumu
dialogues.text: Don't listen to his nonsense. I'm sure you're well aware of the major failings of the Kujou Clan. Surely you of everyone knows — not a single word they say can be trusted!

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Hmph. You are quite mistaken if you think your dispute is of any interest to me. Descendant of the Takatsukasa Clan, you wish to become the new Tenryou Commissioner. Do I understand this correctly?

dialogues.speaker: Takatsukasa Susumu
dialogues.text: Uh, well... y—yes, of course! It's the eternal pursuit of everyone in the Tenryou Commission to offer our lives in service of the Almighty Shogun!

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Then the situation is not as complicated as you seem to have made it. After all, I am the one who appoints the Tenryou Commissioner. The process is quite simple: Anyone who can beat me in a duel becomes the new Commissioner.

dialogues.speaker: Takatsukasa Susumu
dialogues.text: Um, sorry... a duel with the Almighty Shogun?

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: The first Tenryou Commissioner demonstrated his will with the blade in his hand. That is why the title has been passed down within the Kujou Clan ever since.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: If you want me to appoint a new clan, then naturally, there must first be a new duel.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Do you not know how to wield a blade...? Or do you simply doubt your abilities on account of your advanced age and declining physical condition?

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Here you are talking about offering your life, and yet you are too afraid to face my blade?

dialogues.speaker: Takatsukasa Susumu
dialogues.text: Um... Well...

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Well, never mind. What about one of you, then? Anyone who can defeat me, Takatsukasa or not, will be appointed the new Tenryou Commissioner.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Does not a single person dare to face me?

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
dialogues.text: I will challenge you, Almighty Shogun!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whaaat!?

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Descendant of the Kujou Clan. Regrettably, even if you win against me, it cannot atone for the wrongs committed under the Kujou name.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
dialogues.text: I realize that. I don't stand a chance of winning against you anyway. I know full well that the mistakes my father made ought to spell the end of the Kujou Clan's legacy in the Tenryou Commission...

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
dialogues.text: Even when I was executing the Vision Hunt Decree, I had doubts about my father's decisions. I knew that what I was doing was wrong.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
dialogues.text: But that was as far as I went. I doubted, and I ruminated. I understood the situation perfectly well, but I took no action, and I didn't save a single person.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
dialogues.text: I accept the Kujou Clan's decline as punishment for my deeds. I can't even say that I failed to prevent it... because in order to fail, you have to have at least tried.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: To be brutally honest... for someone of your strength, there is nothing you could have done even if you had tried.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
dialogues.text: Yes... I'm too weak. My father ignores me, my elder brother can't help me, and I even need Ippei to set me straight at times... It's the way it's always been...

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
dialogues.text: But if nothing else, then right here, right now, in the Kujou Clan's final hours, it is I who represent the clan, like my father before me! His duties are now mine to perform!

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
dialogues.text: Just as the Shogun said, a forefather of mine once showed his will with his sword...

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
dialogues.text: Then please, let me, Kujou Kamaji, end the story of the Kujou Clan in the same way that it began!

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
dialogues.text: This is my last chance to do something!

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: This is patently meaningless.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: But I accept. Come forward.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: The Kujou Clan's honor was forged with courage, tempered with integrity, and shines beyond life and death

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Kujou Kamaji is wounded. Descendants of the Takatsukasa Clan, it is your responsibility to take care of him.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: You may not have the courage to challenge me, but I trust that you are capable of attending to a small matter such as this.

dialogues.speaker: Takatsukasa Susumu
dialogues.text: Yes, of course. I apologize... I'm sorry. So, so sorry.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: I had heard that the Kujou Clan is no longer fit to shoulder the work of the Tenryou Commission. The search for a successor to the role of Tenryou Commissioner is indeed a matter of great urgency...

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: However, following this duel, I have decided to postpone the Kujou Clan's punishment for the time being.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: In the meantime, I expect the Takatsukasa Clan to continue supporting the Kujou Clan as before.

dialogues.speaker: Takatsukasa Susumu
dialogues.text: As you instruct, so it shall be done. We would not dare question the Almighty Shogun's will.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Finally, if you still think you can copy the Fatui's strategy of providing me with deceptive information to produce flaws in my judgment...

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: ...You will see me appear once again as I have done today — only next time, my blade will show no mercy.

dialogues.speaker: Takatsukasa Susumu
dialogues.text: Understood. Thank you, Almighty Shogun, for your wisdom and mercy!

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: That will do. I will have the Okuzumeshuu continue the investigation from here.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Come with me. Let's find a quiet place. There's something I want to talk about with you.

talks.objective: Follow Ei out of the outpost

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: When it's time to deal with a situation, you're just like the Shogun. So strict.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: You think so? I thought I was rather accommodating. If it had been the Shogun... she would have decapitated Kujou Kamaji without a second thought.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: I do believe he was prepared for that outcome. I could see it in his eyes.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: The Kujou Clan has undergone a dramatic change from its glory days to its present decline. Kamaji is hardly a great heir to the Kujou name, but...

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: He has shown me how some things remain the same even as the world around them changes.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: I also have you to thank. The things we experienced out on the streets and the photo you took of me, they helped me come to this realization, too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So what's next for the Kujou Clan? Will they get to carry on being in charge of the Tenryou Commission?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Not a chance. Even if their heir was someone who showed promise, their past mistakes cannot be erased.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Still... I will give them a little more time. After all, they are not the only ones who have made mistakes.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: The Shogun does not make mistakes — she is incapable of doing so. But I, as Ei, would like to offer my apologies.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: I have much to contemplate in the days to come. But at least I can now see the way ahead.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Will you rule Inazuma directly?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: I think I'll leave that to the Shogun. The greatest threat to eternity is still the erosion that comes with time.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: As I said, the Shogun has a robust system to protect her against modification. This is because I anticipated that I myself would change over time.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: But I've made up my mind. So I will do what needs to be done, no matter how difficult it is.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Mmm...

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: This has certainly been a memorable series of events.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Absolutely! You sorted out the Tenryou Commission and the people in the city got to see a happy and healthy Shogun. All the awful rumors will disappear in no time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If you enjoyed your trip, we should get you out again some time!

choices.text: Next time, we'll bring you some souvenirs.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: No need. There's no place for such things in my life.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Also, please stop making it sound as if I somehow need the company.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Okay, I'm ready to head back now.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: My period of solitude will now continue, but it will not last too much longer. I will leave you humans to deal with any minor issues in the meantime.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, see you next time!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Considering a lot of what happened was pretty unexpected, things seemed to have worked out surprisingly well in the end.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The only thing left to do is return the Pass Permit to Yae Miko.

choices.text: Next time, we'll bring you some fun little trinkets.
Maybe that's what he was expecting.

talks.objective: Give the Pass Permit back to Yae Miko

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Miko, we're back! We had a great trip!

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Did you now? Well then, you'll have to tell me all about it.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Hehe, how amusing. The Almighty Shogun goes downtown and suddenly she's like a wide-eyed country girl trying to find her bearings in the big city. Marvelous.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: What a shame I didn't get to see it for myself.

choices.text: Only you would dare to say that.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: It's fine, she wouldn't mind. Really, she wouldn't.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: So. From what you were saying, it seems that she has finally begun to comprehend what form eternity should take?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: That's the most important outcome of this trip. To be honest, I wasn't expecting you'd make such great progress when I lent you the Pass Permit.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah. It seems like she's not gonna force everything to stay the same way anymore.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: To put it nicely, even deities indulge in wishful thinking. To put it more bluntly, there are things that even The Seven can't do when faced with something even more powerful than themselves.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hehe. Take a guess.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Anyway. It sounds like you had a very pleasant trip and even had the chance to see Ei's less formal side.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Next time you wish to see her, you can come and take the Pass Permit from me again. She would never admit to it, but she does, in fact, get quite lonely.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? But she said she doesn't need company...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Because she is a god. It's not that gods don't need the company of others, just that the idea of a god having company seems indulgent to her.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: But you don't belong to this world. Perhaps you are just the company she needs.

choices.text: You and the Shogun enjoy teasing each other.
